record.original_question: Classify all chiral polytopes of nearly full rank, where in Euclidean d-space this means finite (d-1)-polytopes or infinite d-polytopes.

evidence.quote: Problem 21. Describe all chiral polytopes of nearly full rank.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set of "faces" satisfying the usual diamond, flag-connectedness, and strong flag-connectedness axioms; its automorphism group acts freely on the set of flags. Such a polytope is called chiral if its automorphism group has exactly two orbits on the flags, with any two adjacent flags lying in different orbits (so the polytope admits all combinatorial rotational symmetries but no reflective symmetry). A geometric realization of an abstract n-polytope in Euclidean d-space E^d is a mapping of its faces to (affine) subsets of E^d that respects the face lattice and is compatible with the action of the automorphism group by isometries; the realization is faithful when this mapping is injective on faces and the symmetry group action is faithful. A realization in E^d of an abstract polytope of rank n is said to be of nearly full rank if either (i) the polytope is finite and d = n − 1, or (ii) the polytope is infinite (an apeirotope) and d = n.

Problem. Classify, up to similarity in Euclidean space, all faithful chiral geometric realizations of nearly full rank; that is, determine all finite chiral (d−1)-polytopes faithfully realized in E^d and all infinite chiral d-apeirotopes faithfully realized in E^d, for every dimension d.
artifact.status_search_result: The full classification of chiral polytopes of nearly full rank in Euclidean space does not appear to have been completed. Related results are partial: chiral polytopes of full rank have been shown to exist only in ranks 4 and 5, with specific examples (e.g., Roli's cube in rank 4 and a known chiral 5-polytope of full rank) constructed, while the corresponding nearly full rank classification remains a subject of active research and no comprehensive classification has been published.

status_evidence.title: Chiral polytopes of full rank exist only in ranks 4 and 5
status_evidence.snippet: A chiral polytope of full rank can only have rank 4 or 5.
status_evidence.claim: Full rank chiral case is restricted, but the nearly full rank classification is not addressed here.

status_evidence.title: A chiral 5-polytope of full rank
status_evidence.snippet: First known chiral 5-polytope of full rank presented.
status_evidence.claim: Only isolated examples and the full-rank case are settled; nearly full rank remains open.

status_evidence.title: Quasi-Regular Polytopes of Full Rank
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses realizations of full and nearly full rank for regular/quasi-regular polytopes.
status_evidence.claim: Related classifications exist for regular and quasi-regular cases, but the chiral nearly full rank case is not classified.
